issues.description: The Bitmap24 constructor declaration in the template header declares three parameters (int i_width, int i_height, int depth) but the Bitmap24 implementation defines a constructor with only two parameters (int p_width, int p_height). The solution repository uses a two-parameter constructor. This mismatch between declaration and definition in the template is a structural inconsistency that can confuse students and may lead to compilation or linkage surprises if code expects the three-parameter variant.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the header and implementation consistent. Either (a) change example_program/src/Bitmap24.hpp in the template to declare Bitmap24(int i_width, int i_height) to match the implementation (and the solution), or (b) implement the three-parameter constructor in example_program/src/Bitmap24.cpp (and adjust uses) if a depth argument is intended. Prefer option (a) to match the solution and avoid introducing unused API differences.

issues.description: Constructor signature for the Bitmap24 class is inconsistent between declaration and definition across artifacts: the template repository header declares Bitmap24(int i_width, int i_height, int depth) while the implementation (Bitmap24::Bitmap24) in the same template uses two parameters (int p_width, int p_height). The solution repository uses a two-argument constructor (Bitmap24(int i_width, int i_height)). This mismatch (extra 'depth' parameter in the template header) creates confusion for students and will cause compilation/signature errors or uncertainty about the intended API.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the constructor declaration consistent across artifacts. Remove the extraneous 'depth' parameter from the template header so the declaration becomes Bitmap24(int i_width, int i_height), matching the implementation and the solution. Alternatively, if a depth parameter is intended, update the implementation in both template and solution to define Bitmap24::Bitmap24(int p_width, int p_height, int depth) and update usages accordingly.
